Abstract
               
                  Motivation
                  The computational prediction of RNA secondary structure by free energy minimization has become an important tool in RNA research. However in practice, energy minimization is mostly limited to pseudoknot-free structures or rather simple pseudoknots, not covering many biologically important structures such as kissing hairpins. Algorithms capable of predicting sufficiently complex pseudoknots (for sequences of length n) used to have extreme complexities, e.g. Pknots has O(n6) time and O(n4) space complexity. The algorithm CCJ dramatically improves the asymptotic run time for predicting complex pseudoknots (handling almost all relevant pseudoknots, while being slightly less general than Pknots), but this came at the cost of large constant factors in space and time, which strongly limited its practical application (∼200 bases already require 256 GB space).
               
               
                  Results
                  We present a CCJ-type algorithm, Knotty, that handles the same comprehensive pseudoknot class of structures as CCJ with improved space complexity of Θ(n3+Z)—due to the applied technique of sparsification, the number of ‘candidates’, Z, appears to grow significantly slower than n4 on our benchmark set (which include pseudoknotted RNAs up to 400 nt). In terms of run time over this benchmark, Knotty clearly outperforms Pknots and the original CCJ implementation, CCJ 1.0; Knotty’s space consumption fundamentally improves over CCJ 1.0, being on a par with the space-economic Pknots. By comparing to CCJ 2.0, our unsparsified Knotty variant, we demonstrate the isolated effect of sparsification. Moreover, Knotty employs the state-of-the-art energy model of ‘HotKnots DP09’, which results in superior prediction accuracy over Pknots.
               
               
                  Availability and implementation
                  Our software is available at https://github.com/HosnaJabbari/Knotty.
               
               
                  Supplementary information
                  Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

Abstract

Motivation
Free-energy minimization for predicting RNA secondary structure has become a key method in RNA research. In practice, however, energy minimization is largely confined to pseudoknot-free structures or only very simple pseudoknots, leaving out many biologically important motifs such as kissing hairpins. Methods able to predict sufficiently complex pseudoknots for sequences of length n have historically had extreme complexity; for example, Pknots has O(n6) time and O(n4) space complexity. The CCJ algorithm greatly improves the asymptotic runtime for complex pseudoknot prediction, handling nearly all relevant pseudoknots while being slightly less general than Pknots, but its large constant factors in both time and space severely restrict practical use, with around 200 bases already needing 256 GB of memory.

Results
We introduce Knotty, a CCJ-style algorithm that supports the same broad class of pseudoknotted structures as CCJ but with improved space complexity of Θ(n3+Z). Thanks to sparsification, the number of candidates Z seems to increase much more slowly than n4 on our benchmark set, which includes pseudoknotted RNAs up to 400 nt. On this benchmark, Knotty clearly outperforms Pknots and the original CCJ implementation, CCJ 1.0, in runtime; its memory use is also fundamentally better than CCJ 1.0 and comparable to the space-efficient Pknots. By comparing against CCJ 2.0, our unsparsified Knotty variant, we isolate the effect of sparsification. In addition, Knotty uses the current state-of-the-art energy model, HotKnots DP09, yielding better prediction accuracy than Pknots.

Availability and implementation
The software is available at https://github.com/HosnaJabbari/Knotty.

Supplementary information
Supplementary data are available online at Bioinformatics.
